approach:
Add one reading check, `check_part_coverage(reading, request)`, as one new `step!(check_part_coverage(reading, request));` line placed last in `refusing_check` (checks.rs:546, after check_reading_references). Appending it last means no existing refusing case changes its first refuser. The existing parser (`is_bullet`, `request_text_acceptance`, topics.rs:266-282) is untouched. A new parser `request_parts` in topics.rs reads: (a) numbered parts, as runs 1,2,3.. (at least two) in one of three forms: `(N)` at line start or inline in a paragraph, `N.` at line start, `N)` at line start; and (b) dash or star Acceptance bullets (only those after an `Acceptance` heading when one exists, otherwise all). It skips fenced blocks, `>` quoted lines, quoted or backticked spans (via `without_quoted_spans`, terms.rs:86), generator-written lines (`is_generated_line`, terms.rs:62) and everything after `## Source` in an approval request (the same anchors `plain_request_prose` uses, terms.rs:189-208).

In checks.rs, an item is `covered` when some acceptance criterion shares at least `required = min(2, ceil(n/2))` distinctive stems with it (n is the item's count of distinctive stems). A *distinctive stem* is a token of 4+ letters or digits, with a trailing `s` dropped when longer than 4 chars and cut to 5 chars, that is not in a const stop list. The stop list holds generic gate words such as test, pass, change, described, existing, job, part. Both rules are defined in a code comment and pinned by a unit test. An item with no distinctive stem (`Yes`, `No`) is not checked. The cap at 2 is why the long-title Steward bullet `The change is made as described: <title>` is accepted when the reading restates the title in a few words. Dropping `fmt, clippy and test pass` leaves only the stem `clipp` (test, pass and fmt are stop or too short), so that twin is refused. An item is *deferred* when a sentence of the reading's summary, assumptions, departures or out_of_scope has a deferral phrase (follow-up, deferred, later job, separate job, not in this job and the like), no negation guard ('never', 'without', 'refus', 'unless', 'do not'), and names the item. Naming means a marker reference in the phrase's clause (`(3)`, `part 3`), or the required stem overlap. An out_of_scope item that names the marker `(3)` or `part 3` counts without a phrase. Criteria are never searched for deferral, because a criterion may describe the gate itself. A part or bullet is refused when it is deferred or uncovered, unless the request permits a split.

The split exemption reads only the request's plain sentences (not quoted, fenced or generated). A sentence permits a split only when it has a modal (may, can, could, might, is allowed to), no negation, none of the complaint words (earlier, previous, last, rejected, wrong, said, reading, attempt), and one of two shapes. (1) `<adjective> <noun>`, where the adjective is separate, follow-up (or `follow up`), later, next, smaller, several or multiple and the noun is job, change, PR, request or part. (2) `split` then `into` then (optional determiner) a noun, so `may be split into jobs` passes but `may split checks.rs into modules` does not. Ordinary uses ('split checks.rs into modules', 'test each form separately') and complaints ('the earlier reading said (3) is a follow-up; that was wrong') never match. A permission sentence that names a marker exempts only those parts; one that names none exempts every item.

Fixing the test fixtures this change breaks is part of the change. The fake reader (fake.rs:311) emits one fixed criterion, and the CLI `Scenario` reader (athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs:572) returns `default_reading()` whatever the request says. Requests with bullets, such as drain.rs:3988 and job_plan.rs:166, would now be refused. fake.rs therefore adds one content criterion per request line that is a bullet or numbered part, and `Scenario::script` appends the request's bullet lines the same way. The producer then runs the full `cargo test` and fixes any other fixed-reading fixture at its seam, not by weakening the check.

Corpus input forms mapped to cases (read in refusal_corpus.rs). Existing cases: `numbered-dot-parts` (:1707, number-dot-parts, stays Accept because base_reading copies the bullets); `numbered-paren-parts-not-read-today` (:1721, number-paren-parts, renamed `numbered-paren-parts-uncovered`, now Refuse by check_part_coverage with `bullets_expected` still 0, plus a `-covered` Accept twin); `lettered-paren-parts-not-read-today` (:1734, letter-paren-parts, stays Accept, comment says letters are still not read); `steward-three-dash-bullets` (:1680, dash-bullet) and `star-bullets` (:1695, star-bullet) stay Accept; `root-cause-cites-two-jobs-without-relying` (:1753) and `retry-complaint-reading-names-the-job` / `-omits-the-job` (:1783, :1801) stay as they are. decisions.choice: New check is the last `step!` line; the parser is a new `request_parts`, and `is_bullet`/`request_text_acceptance` are not touched.
decisions.reason: A last step cannot change which check refuses first in any existing corpus or unit case. `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` (corpus :2733) then needs only new refusing cases. `request_text_acceptance` also serves plan_entry, steward and hestia (topics.rs:276), and every corpus case pins its count in `bullets_expected` (corpus :2616).

rejected.why: It would change the first refuser of existing refusing cases.

decisions.choice: Coverage is stem overlap with a cap: required shared distinctive stems = min(2, ceil(n/2)). Distinctive means 4+ chars, trailing s dropped, cut to 5 chars, not in a stop list that includes test, pass, change, described, existing, job, part.
decisions.reason: This is the fix for the earlier major finding 1. The real Steward bullets (steward.rs:621-623) are accepted when the criteria restate them, even with a long title, because the cap stops a long title demanding many words. Generic words cannot cover the 'fmt, clippy and test pass' bullet, so the drop twin is refused. The definition is written in a code comment and pinned by a unit test (the earlier minor finding).

rejected.option: Require every stem of the item to appear.
rejected.why: It refuses the real Steward bullet whenever the reading shortens the title.
Checks cost no model call and must be deterministic (checks.rs docs; the replay passes no model).

rejected.option: One-to-one assignment of criteria to items.
rejected.why: A reading that merges two bullets into one criterion would be refused.

decisions.choice: The split exemption counts only permission phrasing: modal, no negation, no complaint word, and an `<adjective> <noun>` or `split into <noun>` shape. It is tied to the named part when the sentence names one.
decisions.reason: This is the fix for the earlier major finding 2. 'split' and 'separately' in an ordinary sense, and a complaint that quotes the old deferral, must not exempt. Table tests pin both directions.

rejected.option: Exempt when the request contains the word split or separately.
rejected.why: It fires on 'split checks.rs into modules' and 'test each form separately'.

rejected.option: A global exemption for any permission sentence.
rejected.why: 'Part (3) may be split' would also exempt unrelated bullets.

decisions.choice: Deferral is searched in summary, assumptions, departures and out_of_scope, never in criteria. A deferral needs a phrase plus a marker or stem match; out_of_scope with a marker reference counts without a phrase.
decisions.reason: A criterion may describe the gate ('refuses a reading that defers part (3)'). An out_of_scope item such as 'athena.toml' must not defer a bullet that says athena.toml is unchanged.

rejected.option: Search every reading field, including criteria.
rejected.why: It would refuse readings whose criteria test deferral, including this job's own.

decisions.choice: Fix fixed-reading test fixtures at their seams: fake.rs reader_turn and athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs Scenario::script add request bullet lines as criteria.
decisions.reason: fake.rs:311 and common/mod.rs:489-573 return a reading that ignores the request, while drain.rs:3988/4067/4492 and job_plan.rs:166 queue bullet requests. They would be refused by the production path (reading.rs:722). The fake only copies request lines; the logic under test stays in core.

rejected.option: Skip the new check for nested or fake runs.
rejected.why: A bypass would leave the gate untested end to end.
